title: Monitor
unavailable: This server does not provide system metrics.
memSplitHint: Apps is what programs hold (LordOS's own included). System and drivers is what the kernel and the drivers keep for themselves, the graphics card's buffers among them.
memTopHint: Each app's processes added up. Shared memory is split among the processes that share it (your own larger processes); for the others it counts in each one, so these can add up to more than Apps.
cacheHint: The file cache speeds up repeated reads from disks. Linux frees it by itself when an app needs memory, so it does not count as used.
net.disabled: Showing each app's connections is turned off in Settings → Privacy → Monitor.
net.noDiag: The kernel did not answer the socket query (sock_diag).
net.allGood: Nothing blocked. Lumo is on guard.
privacy.title: Monitor
privacy.connectionsHint: Monitor lists your apps' network connections (address, port, state and process). It only reads kernel state; it does not block anything.
privacy.geoHint: Looks up the country of each address in a database shipped with LordOS (DB-IP Lite Country, CC BY 4.0).
privacy.local: Everything is computed on this computer. The live lists only run while Monitor is open; the traffic history, when it is on, is recorded by your session. No IP address leaves the computer.
net.privacyShort: IP-to-country from a local database (DB-IP Lite, CC BY 4.0, db-ip.com): no address leaves the computer.
proc.why.init: This process starts and runs the whole system.
proc.why.kernel: This is part of the Linux kernel.
proc.why.session: This is your LordOS session. To end it, use Log Out from the LordOS menu.
proc.why.system: This process is part of LordOS.
proc.needAdmin: This process belongs to {user}. Only an administrator can stop another user’s processes.
proc.confirm: Are you sure you want to quit “{name}”?
proc.confirmHint: Quit asks it to close. Force Quit stops it at once; any unsaved work in it is lost.
proc.confirmOther: This process belongs to {user}. Quit asks it to close; Force Quit stops it at once.
proc.r.isolated: Isolated LordOS app (Landlock, seccomp, own cgroup)
proc.files.naOwn: Its open files can’t be read.
proc.files.naAdmin: Its open files could not be read.
proc.files.needAdmin: This process belongs to another user. Only an administrator can see its open files and ports.
proc.files.needAdminShort: Only an administrator can see this
proc.files.countCut: Showing {shown} of {count} open files and ports
proc.goneHint: It is no longer running, so there is nothing more to show.
proc.noCmdline: (none: a kernel thread or a process that cleared it)
temp.noSensorHint: This disk has no temperature sensor the system can read (memory cards, virtual disks and many USB adapters don’t).
temp.restingHint: The disk is resting: it is read again as soon as it is used, so it can stay spun down.
temp.limitDefault: Limit {max} °C (the drive does not report its own)
temp.title: Temperature · {name}
health.title: Health (SMART)
health.noneHint: This kind of disk does not report its health (memory cards, virtual disks).
health.standby: The disk is resting: its health is read the next time it is used.
health.errorHint: The disk did not answer SMART (it may not have it, or be behind a USB adapter that blocks it).
health.hint.warning: There are signs of wear: open it in Disks to see why, and keep a backup.
health.hint.failing: The disk says it will fail soon. Copy your data now.
health.hint.unknown: The disk answered, but without enough data.
health.basic: Basic reading. Install smartmontools in Disks for the full report and self-tests.
diskAlert.toggle: Notify me when a disk gets too hot or its health gets worse
diskAlert.hotBody: {dev} is at {temp} °C (limit {max} °C). Check the airflow around it.
diskAlert.checkBody: {dev} shows signs of wear. Make sure you have a backup.
diskAlert.failBody: {dev} reports that it will fail soon. Copy your data now.
health.idle: Not read yet: a spinning disk is read the next time it is in use, so a resting disk is not woken up. With smartmontools it is read without waking it.
hist.unavailable: The traffic history is not available in this session.
hist.off: The traffic history is off (Settings → Privacy → Monitor).
hist.none: Nothing was recorded in this period.
privacy.historyHint: Bytes received and sent per minute for 7 days and per hour for 30 days, for the computer and for each app. Never addresses, names or countries. Kept only in your home folder.
net.remoteNoFailures: No failed sign-ins in the last 24 hours.
net.remoteAdminOnly: Only administrators see failed sign-ins and can block addresses.
net.view.sort.name: Name
net.view.menuItem: Show network activity in the menu bar
net.systemService: Essential system service: shown, never blocked
net.noMatch: Nothing matches the search and the filters
net.noneDenied: Nothing denied in the last ten minutes
net.rangeNote: Traffic of each app in the {range} window. The history keeps only how much each app moved, never where.
comp.mailHint: Mail, Calendar, Contacts and Reminders: their servers, from their own process and scope.
comp.storeHint: The package engine: catalogs, apps and system updates.
comp.storeWarn: While the Store and updates are blocked, LordOS gets no security updates and no app can be installed.
comp.printHint: Network printers and scanners, and their discovery on the local network.
comp.terminalHint: Every program started in the Terminal, with its own name in the list.
comp.listsHint: The daily download of the blocklists you turned on.
comp.vpnHint: The traffic of your VPN tunnels. Manage them in Settings → Network.
comp.dnsHint: The system resolver, which turns names into addresses for every app.
comp.timeHint: Keeps the clock right with time servers.
comp.networkHint: Addresses from the network (DHCP), Wi-Fi and VPN connections.
privacy.menuItem: Network activity in the menu bar
privacy.menuItemHint: Upload and download rates in the menu bar, with recent activity and quick controls.
status.title: Network

net.icmpSockets.one: {count} ICMP (ping) socket: the system doesn't keep its destination
net.icmpSockets.other: {count} ICMP (ping) sockets: the system doesn't keep their destination

net.rawSockets: raw IP sockets ({what}): it can see or forge IP traffic
net.packetSockets: packet sockets ({what}): it can see or forge traffic on the network card
volt.powerNote: The sum of the rails listed below. The real draw is higher: it leaves out USB devices, the fan and regulator losses.
volt.sinceBootNote: From the kernel log, which keeps its most recent messages only.
volt.lastAt: The last one {h} h {m} min after boot.
volt.window: Last 5 minutes while this view is open
volt.rawNote: Inputs with no label are the value at the chip's pin, before the board's scaling. They are not the voltage of a rail.
volt.explain.normal: The board's under-voltage alarm is off.
volt.explain.low: The 5 V input is under {low} V. The board's alarm is off, but the power supply or its cable may be too weak.
volt.explain.under: The board itself reports under-voltage: it may slow down or lose data. Use a stronger power supply or a shorter cable.
volt.explain.happened: The board reported under-voltage earlier and it is fine now. Heavy load or a USB device may have caused it.
comp.lanHint: Files → Network: computers and shares on the local network.
comp.machinesHint: Machines: the network traffic of the virtual machines you run, the systems you download in the New Machine assistant, and their checksum lists. A rule for Machines applies to all of them.
gpu.title: GPU
gpu.none: This computer has no graphics processor that LordOS can read: drawing is done by the processor.
gpu.loadFromApps: This driver doesn’t report its load: this is the busiest engine, added up over your apps.
gpu.loadUnknown: This driver doesn’t report its load.
gpu.noApps: No app is using the GPU right now
gpu.appsHint: Your apps only: each engine’s share of the last second and the graphics memory they hold. Other users’ processes and sandboxed helpers can’t be read.
gpu.apisHint: From the drivers installed for this card (nothing is loaded to find out). WebGPU comes with browsers, on top of Vulkan.
gpu.apiState.kfdOnly: The kernel is ready; the runtime isn’t installed
gpu.nothingToChart: This card reports no load, temperature or fan to chart.
gpu.gtt: System memory the card is using: {used} of {total}
gpu.sharedMemory: This GPU shares the computer’s memory: its use is part of Memory.
gpu.noMemory: This driver doesn’t report its memory.
gpu.fan.title: Graphics card fan
gpu.fan.hint: Automatic lets the card decide. By hand it never goes below {floor} %, and it goes back to automatic above {c} °C, when you log out and when the computer restarts.
gpu.fan.adminOnly: Only an administrator can set this fan by hand.
gpu.fan.reverted.hot: It went back to automatic: the card passed {c} °C.
gpu.fan.reverted.error: It went back to automatic: the card stopped answering.
gpu.fan.reverted.session: It went back to automatic: the session that set it ended.
gpu.ai.title: AI
gpu.ai.none: No AI engine is using the GPU right now
gpu.ai.memHidden: its graphics memory is hidden: it runs isolated
gpu.ai.noModels: No voice model is installed (Settings → AI → Voice).
comp.sqlHint: Databases: connections to MySQL and MariaDB servers in your favorites.
